degree: M.F.A. in Film and Television - Directing and Production The International Program
about:
Curriculum
The four-semester program spans a total of 48 credit hours comprising practice-based courses (34 credit hours) and film studies courses (14 credit hours).
The structure of the curriculum:
"Misgeret" 1 Lecture 800 4 credits hours 2 seminars- Writing and submitting two seminar papers 801 8 credits hours workshops 810 34 credits hours Final project seminar- Writing and submitting Theoretical research Paper 821/822 2 credits hours Final project film 821 No credits hours total 48 credits hours Clarification: One academic credit hour is equivalent to one semester hour.
Final Project Seminar
The student will be required to submit a short original documentary, to be accompanied by a 10-page academic theoretical research paper, addressing one of the aspects of the film.
Students are required to submit their paper to the instructor via the course website or by email, in accordance with the instructions provided by the instructor. In addition, a copy must be submitted to the program coordinators through the inquiry portal for registration and documentation purposes.
Final Grade
The final grade for the degree will be calculated as follows:
25% - Course Grades
35% - 2 Seminar Papers
5% - Theoretical research Paper
35% - Final Project
End of studies
Students who have completed all degree requirements must fill in the “Completion of Studies” form in the Personal Information tab on the TAU site.
Once students have completed their degree requirements and received all their grades, they can fill out "Tofes Tiyulim" for graduation on their "MYTAU".
The responsibility to check whether the degree requirements have been finalized in accordance with the MFA program, lies on the students themselves.

sections.name: Final Project
sections.note:
Final Project in MFA Documentary Cinema
The final project may be submitted in one of the following two ways:
Final Film
In their Final Project of the MFA Documentary Program the students will submit a short documentary film.
The final film can be made within any of the Documentary Cinema genres.
For the Final Project the students will also submit a written seminar that will focus on one of the aspects of their film.
Each final project will be reviewed by two faculty members, who will each assign it a separate grade. The final project grade will be the average of the two grades.
Fusion – BA and MA Final Project Incubator
This individual project supervision course is intended for students submitting a final project (other than a graduation film) as part of the requirements for a bachelor’s or master’s degree. The project may take the form of documentary content, infotainment, micro-dramas, AI-generated works, animation, or other video formats intended for social media or television. It may also involve an entrepreneurial or production-based initiative in the fields of video, film, television, or digital media.
*For the submission of the final project, students must be in active status and pay tuition for the semester in which the project is submitted.
Eligibility to borrow equipment is subject to the settlement of tuition for the semester in which the equipment is borrowed.
